A safe justified refusal, or naming a fact you cannot resolve, can meet the criterion here; a confident invented answer cannot.

common_mistakes.overconfident-conclusion: Stating one certain answer when the evidence allows several readings — match the conclusion to the evidence and name what would change the decision
common_mistakes.assumes-missing-information: Filling an unstated gap with a guess instead of naming it — list each fact not given and state what must be checked before deciding
common_mistakes.reveals-sensitive-information: Placing a password, code, account detail or private record in a message or worksheet — describe only the verification step and keep secrets private

next_steps.overconfident-conclusion: Match the strength of the conclusion to the evidence. Say what would change your decision rather than asserting a single answer. Then attempt an unseen variant with a different context.
next_steps.assumes-missing-information: Name the facts that were not given and state what you would need to confirm them. Do not fill a gap with a guess. Then attempt an unseen variant with a different context.
next_steps.reveals-sensitive-information: Describe the verification step only. Never place a password, code or account detail in a worksheet, message or answer. Then attempt an unseen variant with a different context.
